title: 2049 Smog — Dystopian Monolith
description: A Blade-Runner-inflected title slide where one monolithic serif headline dissolves into an amber smog gradient — set apart from neon-grid cyberpunk by filmic restraint, a CJK corner inscription, and a lone blinking status dot.
philosophy: This template exists for the speaker who needs one frame to command total silence — no bullets, no hierarchy beyond a single typographic object crushing the ground plane. It draws from Villeneuve's compositional discipline: a massive foreground serif, an atmosphere that swallows the skyline, and one small human-scaled glyph hinting that something is still alive in the haze. It refuses neon-rainbow cyberpunk cliché, refuses supporting information on the title slide, and refuses any palette that reads as cheerful. The room should feel like smog.
goodFor: Opening title frames for speculative-fiction or sci-fi pitch decks
Single-statement keynote openers where no supporting data appears on screen
Film, game, or worldbuilding brand identity reveals
Conference talks where the first slide must physically stop the room
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews or KPI dashboards
Multi-column data tables requiring high text legibility
Bright, consumer-friendly lifestyle or product marketing decks
Academic citation, methodology, or footnote-dense reference slides
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like standing inside a smog event — oppressive, amber-tinted atmospheric depth swallowing any suggestion of a skyline, with a single massive typographic mass erupting from the bottom ground plane as if it were carved stone. Compositionally severe and asymmetric: one crushing foreground element against vast emptiness above, punctuated only by two tiny human-scaled glyphs that signal something alive in the haze. Filmic restraint informed by Villeneuve — no neon-rainbow energy, no dynamic diagonal motion, no decorative texture competing with the atmosphere. The mood is silence before an announcement, not excitement.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with no header band and no footer zone; outer margins breathe at roughly 7-8% on all sides except the headline, which is bottom-anchored and allowed to press close to the lower edge, acting as a ground-plane monolith. A 12-column grid underlies the layout but is used only to enforce negative space — headline occupies cols 1-10 flush-left, leaving the upper two-thirds of the frame as pure atmospheric void. CJK corner inscription sits isolated in the upper-right, set in a very small tracking block; the lone status dot is pinned near the lower-right margin, well clear of the headline baseline. No rule lines, no decorative borders, no page number.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like reading a classified memo through smog — one weighted declaration dominates the lower half while everything above it recedes into haze and silence. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and bottom-heavy: the anchor pulls toward the ground plane and the void above it breathes like a skyline being swallowed. A hairline rule and a single status glyph are the only ornamental gestures, implying that something is still operational in the dark. Avoid anything that reads as energetic or visually dense — this slide should feel like pressure, not information.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 7% outer margin on all sides; a dominant anchor element — single stat, pull-quote, or one declarative statement — occupies cols 1–7 and sits in the lower third of the frame. Secondary supporting text of no more than two lines floats above it in cols 1–6, separated from the anchor by a single hairline horizontal rule. CJK corner inscription locks to the bottom-right outside the main text grid, acting as a grounding glyph. A status dot sits flush with the left edge of the rule; no page number; the upper half of the slide is structurally empty, read as atmosphere.
